reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be any normed additive commutative group whose closed metric balls are compact, and let f:E→ℝ be continuous. For every global minimizer z of f, every center x₀∈E, and all real numbers R>0 and ε>0 such that ‖z−x₀‖≤R, define δ=ε/R² and W(x)=f(x)+(δ/2)‖x−x₀‖² for x∈E. There exists w∈E such that W(w)≤W(x) for every x∈E, ‖w−x₀‖≤‖z−x₀‖, and, for every x∈E, the inequality W(x)−W(w)≤ε/2 implies f(x)−f(z)≤ε. The same chosen w satisfies both the distance bound and the implication for all x.
notes: The ambient object requires only a proper normed additive commutative group, not a real vector space. Both minima are global and attained. No uniqueness, differentiability, convexity, or probabilistic assumption is stated. The constants are exactly δ=ε/R², quadratic coefficient δ/2, and regularized suboptimality threshold ε/2; the original objective tolerance is ε.
